item.title: What an economics Nobel Prize winner knows about pricing
item.description: NPR's Ailsa Chang chats with Michael Woodford of Columbia University, who was one of two Americans awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics.

item.title: Naturalization in the U.S. is on the decline
item.description: The number of naturalization ceremonies for would-be American citizens is on the decline. This year, ceremonies have been canceled and citizenship applications face increased scrutiny and delays.
item.content:encoded: The number of naturalization ceremonies for would-be American citizens is on the decline.  This year, ceremonies have been canceled and citizenship applications face increased scrutiny and delays.

item.title: Bipartisan group of senators call on Trump to rescind Russian diesel deal
item.description: Six Democratic and six Republican senators wrote a letter calling on President Trump to withdraw from his recent deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

item.title: A judge blocks the government's tree-clearing spree at a municipal D.C. golf course
item.description: Locals and preservationists have long opposed Trump's plan to redevelop a municipal D.C. golf course. That legal fight escalated after the government cleared hundreds of trees on short notice.

item.title: Cornell University bans frat parties, vows to address 'disturbing' campus culture
item.description: In a letter, Cornell's president apologized for what happened to the student who alleges she was raped by several men at a fraternity house in 2024 and promised 'meaningful action.'

item.title: Voters here will decide whether to force cities to build cheaper, smaller homes
item.description: Voters in Massachusetts will decide whether to require cities and towns to allow smaller homes on smaller lots. A growing number of states are doing the same to help ease a housing shortage.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Win or lose, independent candidates want to meet voters in the middle
item.description: Nearly 200 independent candidates in more than 100 congressional races are trying to prove there's an alternative to the two party system — even though the chance of winning is very low.

item.title: Polls are a snapshot, and other helpful things to remember during the midterm elections
item.description: With Election Day just a few weeks away — and millions of votes already cast — midterm polls are everywhere. While polling can be a helpful tool to understand the electorate, it's not a crystal ball.

item.title: Some of the most pristine coral reefs have a secret weapon: birds
item.description: Coral reefs are facing increasing threats around the globe. But on a remote Pacific island, scientists have found that reefs can get help from a surprising ally: seabirds.

item.title: Federal agents search Rep. Ilhan Omar's DC home
item.description: Federal agents searched the Washington, D.C. home of Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., Monday morning. Omar criticized the search, calling it a weaponization of federal law enforcement.
